category_title: Student with TBI who makes disrespectful comments and draws during work
minimal_context: Zeke is assigned an independent math worksheet in the pull-out special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your independent math worksheet. Please complete these problems on your own.

STUDENT: I don't even have a pencil or anything to write with.

TUTOR: Here is a pencil. Go ahead and start working.

STUDENT: (Takes the pencil and starts drawing pictures on the desk) This work is stupid and I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: Please stop drawing and focus on your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Turns to a classmate sitting nearby) What are you looking at? Mind your own business or I'll punch you in the face.

options.A: Develop critical consciousness through genuine multicultural math curricula addressing authentic issues of race, ethnicity, social class, and disability, acknowledging realities from various positionalities.
options.B: Provide access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during independent math assignments by giving the student a squishy, stress-relief ball.
options.C: Use basketball references from LeBron James, music from popular rappers, or local skateboarding references to engage the student during independent math worksheets.
options.D: Provide easy tasks consisting of independent math assignments selected by the teacher that the student, without assistance, is likely to complete with 80% or better accuracy.
